standard.title: Acknowledge and extend in discussion
standard.description: listen for key points and information to carry out tasks and contribute to discussions, acknowledging another opinion, linking a response to the topic, and sharing and extending ideas and information
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions, sharing information and ideas (AC9E3LY02). They have not yet practised acknowledging another's opinion and linking responses to the topic while extending ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can listen for key points in a discussion, acknowledge another's opinion, link their response to the topic, and share ideas that extend or build on what others have contributed.

nodes.label: Listening for key points
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify key points and information in what others say in a discussion and use these in their own contribution.
nodes.minimum_width: After listening to a peer's contribution, identify one key point and reference it in a follow-up response.
nodes.typical_width: Listen actively across a discussion, taking notes or tracking key points, and reference what others have said in own contributions to demonstrate listening and build coherence in the discussion.
wider: Practise active listening in structured discussion formats (Socratic seminar, fishbowl) where referencing others' ideas is required
Reflect on one's own listening after a discussion, identifying what was easy and difficult to track and why
nodes.hinge_reason: Acknowledging another's opinion in N2 requires students to have identified key points from that contribution — N2 cannot be performed without N1's active listening.

response_modes.reason: Active listening while tracking key points is a fluency habit requiring repeated practice across different discussion contexts before students can reliably identify what to reference.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one key point from another person's contribution
Can reference that point in their own response

nodes.label: Acknowledging and extending
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use language that acknowledges another's opinion and links their own response to the topic while extending or building on what was said.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one acknowledgement phrase ('I agree with... because...' or 'I see it differently because...') in a discussion contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of discussion language that acknowledges, extends, questions and links — including phrases that agree, partially agree, respectfully disagree and build on — across different types of classroom discussion.
wider: Compare formal discussion language conventions across different contexts (class meeting, debate, book club) and explain how the formality affects language choices
Examine how discussion skills differ across cultures and explore culturally appropriate ways to acknowledge and extend ideas

response_modes.reason: Extending another's idea rather than just starting a new thread is a discipline that requires sustained practice. Students need repeated structured opportunities across different discussion contexts.

success_criteria: Uses at least one acknowledgement phrase in a discussion contribution
Links own contribution to the topic rather than introducing an unrelated idea
